hints: Focus on what gas is actually made when an acid reacts with a reactive metal, and what controls how much of it forms.
Work out the moles of propanoic acid first, using $M_r = 74$ for $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ and $3.70$ g.
Write both equations and compare how many moles of acid are needed for one mole of hydrogen in each case, then convert to volume at s.t.p.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of propanoic acid**

Both samples are identical, so start with the acid. Propanoic acid is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$ with $M_r = 74$.

$$n = \frac{m}{M_r} = \frac{3.70}{74.0} = 0.0500 \text{ mol}$$

**Write both metal-acid equations**

Both metals are in excess, so the acid limits the hydrogen formed. Notice both reactions need 2 acids for 1 hydrogen.

$$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH} + \text{Mg} \rightarrow (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COO})_2\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Calculate moles and volume of hydrogen**

A 2 to 1 ratio means half as many moles of $\text{H}_2$ as acid in both cases.

$$n(\text{H}_2) = \frac{0.0500}{2} = 0.0250 \text{ mol}$$
At s.t.p., 1 mol gas = $22400 \text{ cm}^3$, so:
$$V = 0.0250 \times 22400 = 560 \text{ cm}^3$$
Both reactions give the same $560 \text{ cm}^3$.

options.A: Correct. 0.05 mol acid gives 0.025 mol $\text{H}_2$ in both reactions because both have a 2:1 acid to hydrogen ratio. This is $560 \text{ cm}^3$ at s.t.p. for magnesium and for sodium.
options.B: Incorrect. Sodium does not give twice the hydrogen. Students choose this by thinking 2 Na atoms means 2 $\text{H}_2$, but the balanced equation $2\text{RCOOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2$ still shows only 1 $\text{H}_2$ per 2 acids.
options.C: Incorrect. Magnesium does not give twice the hydrogen. Students choose this by confusing valency with gas amount, but $\text{Mg} + 2\text{RCOOH} \rightarrow (\text{RCOO})_2\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2$ also gives only 1 $\text{H}_2$ per 2 acids.
options.D: Incorrect. This doubles the correct volume. It comes from using a 1:1 acid to hydrogen ratio, forgetting that each $\text{H}_2$ needs two $\text{H}^+$ ions from two $\text{COOH}$ groups.
